source.title: Regularization by Misclassification in ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: E. Cornacchia; Jan Hązła; Ido Nachum; A. Yehudayoff

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how label noise and label smoothing affect test error and activation sparsity, a regularization condition outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported test-error and test-accuracy comparisons and their activation-sparsity measurements are included. The paper's cited results from other work and figure-only values that the text does not describe are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures activation sparsity and generalization under label noise or label smoothing, which none of V1–V8 names. Its random labels are resampled at each training step, unlike V1's fixed random labels. It reports no width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example-removal comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: across the explored settings, label noise or label smoothing induces sparser activations; label noise improves test error in some experiments, while CIFAR-10 accuracy is reported as approximately similar. The conclusion also highlights sparsification during ordinary MNIST training and asks whether SGD itself favors sparse activation patterns.
record.recipe_differences: Studies label noise and label smoothing as training interventions, rather than the original claim's random-label memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, size, sharpness, or memorized-example comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested outcome varies with dataset and intervention: on the hypercube task and MNIST, label noise accompanies lower test error; on CIFAR-10, label smoothing yields similar reported accuracy while reducing penultimate-layer activity.

fits_no_version.finding: Label noise reduces hypercube test error from 49% to 21% and qualitatively improves MNIST test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resampling some labels during training can improve generalization in particular tasks and training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Label noise reduces typical active-neuron counts on the hypercube task and active fractions on MNIST; label smoothing reduces CIFAR-10 penultimate-layer activity from 46.9% to 27.5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise and label smoothing can induce sparser activation patterns in ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 accuracy is reported as slightly above 92% both with and without label smoothing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label smoothing can sparsify activations while preserving approximately similar reported test accuracy in this ResNet-20 setting.

record.problems: The MNIST test-error comparison is described qualitatively and shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. CIFAR-10 accuracy is reported only as 'slightly more than 92%' for both conditions. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No other text-described test-error or test-accuracy comparisons were found. Pure-label-noise decay and firing results concern network death under random labels and do not report the natural-label generalization gap; they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test-error behavior when width increases beyond that needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effects on held-out error and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row measures an outcome outside those versions. No version-specific verdicts are warranted. The pure-noise decay results are declared in rows_left_out and do not test fixed-random-label memorization.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels, or report held-out accuracy on random labels.
Does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on images.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes or large-batch training recipes.
Tests label noise and label smoothing, not dropout or removing dropout and weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or compare their removal with random-example removal.

rows.note: The paper gives 25% versus 6% as the sparsity comparison.
rows.check: The condition assignment is reversed. These percentages describe active neurons: approximately 25% without noise versus 6% with noise. The conclusion explicitly identifies 25% as the final active fraction without noise; Figure 5a supports the direction. Activation sparsity bears on no listed version.
